title: New Research Shows Early Warning Signs for Bowel Disease
subtitle: Scientists discover that blood tests may predict inflammatory bowel disease years before patients feel sick.

summary.en: Researchers have found that the immune system shows warning signs up to ten years before a diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease. By studying blood samples, scientists identified specific antibodies that appear long before symptoms start. This discovery could change how doctors treat conditions like Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis. Currently, these diseases are often treated only after significant damage to the gut has already occurred. Experts hope this research will eventually lead to early prevention and better health outcomes for patients.
summary.zh: 研究人員發現，免疫系統在發炎性腸道疾病確診前十年，就會出現警示訊號。透過研究血液樣本，科學家識別出在症狀出現前就已存在的特定抗體。這項發現可能改變醫師治療克隆氏症與潰瘍性結腸炎等疾病的方式。目前，這些疾病通常是在腸道已受到顯著損害後才進行治療。專家希望這項研究最終能引領早期預防，並為患者帶來更好的健康成果。

paragraphs.en: A group of scientists has discovered a way to potentially identify inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) a decade before patients show any symptoms. This new research offers hope that doctors might one day be able to stop the disease before it causes serious damage to the body. IBD includes two main conditions: Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis. Both cause long-term inflammation in the digestive system, which can lead to severe pain, tiredness, and stomach problems.
paragraphs.zh: 一群科學家發現了一種方法，可能在患者出現任何症狀的十年前，就識別出發炎性腸道疾病（IBD）。這項新研究帶來了希望，未來醫師或許能在疾病對身體造成嚴重損害前就將其阻斷。發炎性腸道疾病包含兩種主要病症：克隆氏症與潰瘍性結腸炎。兩者都會導致消化系統長期發炎，進而引發劇烈疼痛、疲勞與腸胃問題。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian Health, at least 3.8 million people around the world live with these conditions. Currently, doctors usually only start treatment after a patient begins to feel ill. By that time, the gut has often already suffered physical damage. Many patients need strong medicine to control their immune systems, and some eventually require surgery to remove damaged parts of their bowel. Because long-term inflammation can also increase the risk of bowel cancer, finding the disease early is a major goal for medical experts.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報健康》（The Guardian Health）報導，全球至少有三百八十萬人深受這些病症所苦。目前，醫師通常只在患者開始感到不適後才展開治療。到了那個階段，腸道往往已經受到實質損害。許多患者需要強效藥物來控制免疫系統，有些人最終甚至需要透過手術切除受損的腸道部位。由於長期發炎也會增加罹患腸癌的風險，因此提早發現疾病是醫學專家的一大目標。

paragraphs.en: Dr. Arno Bourgonje, a researcher at the University Medical Centre Groningen and the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, explained the importance of this work. He noted that for a long time, doctors could only treat the disease after the damage was already done. The new study shows that the immune system begins to react years before a person feels sick. While this is not yet a test that can tell someone for sure that they will get ill, it is a very important step toward catching the disease early.
paragraphs.zh: 格羅寧根大學醫學中心（University Medical Centre Groningen）與西奈山伊坎醫學院（Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai）的研究員阿諾·布爾貢傑博士（Dr. Arno Bourgonje）解釋了這項研究的重要性。他指出，長期以來，醫師只能在損害發生後才進行治療。這項新研究顯示，免疫系統在患者感到不適的數年前就已開始反應。雖然這還不是一項能確診某人未來一定會發病的檢測，但這已是邁向早期發現疾病極為重要的一步。

paragraphs.en: To reach these findings, the research team studied blood samples from 500 people in the United States military. They looked at 2,000 samples in total. Among these people, 200 later developed Crohn’s disease, 200 developed ulcerative colitis, and 100 did not develop either condition. The scientists screened the blood for antibodies. Antibodies are proteins that the immune system creates to fight off things like bacteria, viruses, or even parts of the body’s own tissues.
paragraphs.zh: 為了達成這些發現，研究團隊分析了五百名美國軍人的血液樣本，總計檢視了兩千份樣本。在這些人當中，有兩百人後來罹患克隆氏症，兩百人罹患潰瘍性結腸炎，另外一百人則未罹患上述任何一種疾病。科學家篩檢了血液中的抗體。抗體是免疫系統為了對抗細菌、病毒，甚至是身體自身組織等外來物所產生的蛋白質。

paragraphs.en: The study, which was published in the journal Gut and presented at a meeting in Barcelona, found clear patterns in the blood. For those who later developed Crohn’s disease, there were higher levels of antibodies against the Epstein-Barr virus, which is the virus that causes glandular fever. These signs were visible ten years before the patients were actually diagnosed. The signals were even stronger in patients who eventually had more severe cases of the disease.
paragraphs.zh: 這項發表於《腸道》（Gut）期刊並在巴塞隆納一場會議上提出的研究，在血液中發現了明確的模式。對於後來罹患克隆氏症的患者，其體內對抗愛潑斯坦-巴爾病毒（Epstein-Barr virus，即導致腺熱的病毒）的抗體濃度較高。這些跡象在患者實際確診的十年前就已顯現。而在最終病情較嚴重的患者身上，這些訊號甚至更為強烈。

paragraphs.en: Patients who developed ulcerative colitis showed a different set of warning signs, including antibodies that reacted against one of the body’s own proteins. This suggests that the immune system is acting in different ways depending on which type of bowel disease a person might develop. James Lindsay, a professor of gastroenterology at Barts Health, who was not part of the research team, said the study provided important new information about the causes of Crohn’s disease.
paragraphs.zh: 罹患潰瘍性結腸炎的患者則呈現出另一組警示訊號，包括對身體其中一種蛋白質產生反應的抗體。這顯示免疫系統會根據個人可能罹患的腸道疾病類型，以不同方式運作。並未參與該研究團隊的巴茲健康（Barts Health）腸胃科教授詹姆斯·林賽（James Lindsay）表示，這項研究為克隆氏症的成因提供了重要的新資訊。

paragraphs.en: While these results are exciting, the researchers warn that more work is needed. The findings must be confirmed in other groups of people to make sure the results are accurate for everyone. Furthermore, the study shows a link between these antibodies and the disease, but it does not prove that the infections themselves are the cause of IBD. Genetics and the tiny microbes living in the gut also play a role in how these diseases start.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管這些結果令人振奮，研究人員仍提醒還需要更多研究。這些發現必須在其他群體中進行驗證，以確保結果對所有人皆準確。此外，該研究顯示了這些抗體與疾病之間的關聯，但並未證明感染本身就是發炎性腸道疾病的成因。遺傳基因以及居住在腸道中的微小微生物，在這些疾病的發病過程中也扮演了角色。

paragraphs.en: Despite these questions, the medical community is optimistic. The researchers hope that IBD could eventually be managed like type 1 diabetes. With diabetes, doctors can use blood tests to see if the immune system has begun to attack the pancreas before any symptoms appear. This allows doctors to start treatments that can delay the start of the disease. If a similar test can be created for IBD, it could change the lives of millions of people, allowing them to receive care long before their health is seriously affected.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管存在這些疑問，醫學界仍持樂觀態度。研究人員希望發炎性腸道疾病最終能像第一型糖尿病一樣受到控制。在糖尿病方面，醫師可以透過血液檢測，在任何症狀出現前觀察免疫系統是否已開始攻擊胰臟。這讓醫師能及早開始治療，進而延緩疾病的發作。如果能為發炎性腸道疾病開發出類似的檢測，將能改變數百萬人的生活，讓他們在健康受到嚴重影響前就能獲得照護。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To display symptoms or signs of a medical condition.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「展示」，這裡指身體出現病徵。文中：a decade before patients show any symptoms.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To resist or defend against an illness or infection.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To cause physical harm or injury to a part of the body.

sources.title: Warning signs could predict inflammatory bowel disease a decade before diagnosis

quiz.question: What specific observation did researchers make regarding patients who later developed Crohn’s disease?

options.A: They had lower levels of antibodies against the Epstein-Barr virus.
options.B: They showed elevated levels of antibodies related to the Epstein-Barr virus a decade before diagnosis.
options.C: They displayed signs of severe glandular fever exactly ten years before symptoms appeared.
options.D: They lacked the body proteins that were found in patients with ulcerative colitis.

quiz.explanationZh: 根據文章第五段，研究發現後來罹患克隆氏症（Crohn’s disease）的患者，在確診前十年，體內對抗 Epstein-Barr 病毒的抗體水平較高。選項 A 與原文相反；選項 C 錯誤，因為文章提到的是抗體跡象，而非確診為腺熱；選項 D 雖然提到潰瘍性結腸炎與蛋白質有關，但並非克隆氏症患者的特徵。

quiz.question: Based on the article, what can be inferred about the current approach to treating inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)?

options.A: It is highly effective at preventing long-term damage to the gut.
options.B: It focuses on early intervention rather than managing existing symptoms.
options.C: It is often reactive, beginning only after the patient's physical health has already declined.
options.D: It relies primarily on diet and lifestyle changes rather than medical procedures.

quiz.explanationZh: 根據第二段與第三段，目前的醫療模式通常是在患者感到不適後才開始治療，此時腸道往往已受損。因此推論出目前的治療是被動的（reactive）。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章提到治療時腸道常已受損；選項 B 與原文描述的現狀相反；選項 D 原文未提及飲食調整為主要治療手段。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the word 'managed' mean in the context of treating IBD like type 1 diabetes?

options.A: Controlled and kept under supervision through ongoing medical care.
options.B: Cured completely so that the patient no longer needs medication.
options.C: Organized by a team of doctors to perform surgery.
options.D: Hidden from the patient to prevent unnecessary stress.

quiz.explanationZh: 在最後一段中，將 IBD 比作第一型糖尿病來「managed」，意指透過持續的監控與治療來控制病情，而非根治。選項 B 錯誤，糖尿病無法根治；選項 C 將管理解釋為組織手術過於狹隘；選項 D 與醫療倫理及文章內容完全無關。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article?

options.A: Scientists have successfully created a definitive test that predicts IBD with 100% accuracy.
options.B: The Epstein-Barr virus is officially confirmed as the sole cause of all inflammatory bowel diseases.
options.C: New research into immune system signals offers a promising path toward early detection and better management of IBD.
options.D: Patients with IBD should stop taking medication and wait for newer research to be published.

quiz.explanationZh: 本文的核心在於介紹一項新研究，該研究透過血液抗體分析，發現了在症狀出現前多年即可偵測到的免疫反應，這為未來早期診斷與預防 IBD 帶來了希望。選項 A 錯誤，文章強調這還不是確診測試；選項 B 錯誤，文章明確表示尚未證實感染是唯一病因；選項 D 則是錯誤的醫療建議。
